# lila.stream

Scene changes as deltas: one message per command or undo step, the same messages the change stream server sends.

```
from lila import stream

def changed(msg):
    if msg["type"] == "group":
        for c in msg["changes"]:
            print(msg["command"], c["kind"], c.get("path"), c.get("attr"))

sub = stream.subscribe(changed, types=["transform"], attrs=["translate"])
stream.unsubscribe(sub)
```

Messages are dicts with a "type": group, resync (ask for a snapshot), event (sceneSaved and the like), snapshot, and with the matching options live and frame. The handler runs on the main thread after each command. Subscriptions made while an extension loads belong to it and go when it unloads. lila.ops.changeStream serves the same stream to other processes over TCP.

## snapshot

```python
snapshot(types=None, attrs=None, under=None, full=False, world=False, evaluated=False)
```

The whole scene as a snapshot message: nodes with their attrs (world matrices with world, evaluated outputs as "outputs" with evaluated), connections, selection and time. Messages with a seq at or below its seq are already in it.

## subscribe

```python
subscribe(fn, types=None, attrs=None, under=None, full=False, live=False, world=False, evaluated=False, owner=None)
```

Call fn(message) for each change message. Returns an id for unsubscribe.

types: node type names (subtypes match). attrs: attribute long names. under: full paths; the node and everything below it. full: whole meshes and large data instead of summaries. live: "live" messages with interim values while a drag is still going. world: "world" changes with the evaluated world matrix of each moved transform and those under it. evaluated: "evaluated" changes with each output (and each connection-driven input) whose evaluated value changed, a mesh's outMesh say. What time moves arrives in "frame" messages, with world or evaluated.

## unsubscribe

```python
unsubscribe(id)
```

False when id is not subscribed.
